content.text: {"primary_meaning": "In Christian teaching, 'instruction' is most commonly understood as divine teaching—God's word and guidance for righteous living. This tracks the Hebrew terms torah (teaching/law/instruction) and musar (instruction/discipline), so 'instruction' is regularly presented as God's revealed will communicated through Scripture, wisdom teaching, and parental/spiritual authority, functioning as the path to life and the beginning of wisdom.", "primary_basis": ["Proverbs 1:7-8 ('fools despise wisdom and instruction... hear, my son, your father's instruction')", "Proverbs 4:13 ('Take hold of instruction; do not let go. Guard her, for she is your life')", "Proverbs 3:11-12 (do not despise the LORD's discipline/instruction)", "Psalm 119 (extended meditation on God's law/instruction as guidance and light, e.g., 119:105)", "Isaiah 2:3 ('out of Zion shall go forth the law/torah, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem')", "Deuteronomy 6:6-7 (commands to be taught diligently to children)", "2 Timothy 3:16 (Scripture profitable for teaching, reproof, correction, and training/instruction in righteousness)"], "alternatives": [{"meaning": "Instruction as fatherly discipline or chastening (musar): God's corrective dealings with believers understood as evidence of sonship and love rather than as verbal teaching.", "basis": ["Proverbs 3:11-12", "Hebrews 12:5-11", "Job 5:17", "Revelation 3:19"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Instruction identified specifically with the Torah/Mosaic Law, read typologically or covenantally as pointing to and fulfilled in Christ.", "basis": ["Matthew 5:17-18", "Galatians 3:24 (the law as tutor/pedagogue leading to Christ)", "Romans 10:4", "John 1:17"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Instruction as the voice of personified Wisdom (and ultimately Christ as the embodiment of divine wisdom/instruction), where receiving instruction symbolizes receiving Christ himself.", "basis": ["Proverbs 8:1-11, 32-36", "Proverbs 9:1-6", "1 Corinthians 1:24, 30", "Matthew 11:28-29 ('learn from me')"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Instruction rendered through associated symbols such as light, a lamp, or a path—i.e., interpreters treating light/way imagery as the symbolic vehicle for divine instruction.", "basis": ["Psalm 119:105", "Proverbs 6:23 ('the commandment is a lamp and the teaching a light')", "Isaiah 8:20"], "prominence": "minority"}], "has_settled_consensus": false, "confidence": "medium", "notes": "'Instruction' functions in Scripture primarily as a concept rather than a symbol proper (unlike leaven, water, or a lamb). It does not appear as a standard entry with a fixed symbolic meaning in most dictionaries of biblical symbolism. There is broad, recognizable agreement that biblical 'instruction' denotes God's teaching/word (torah) and fatherly discipline (musar), but this is closer to lexical-theological consensus than to a settled symbolic interpretation. Any author assigning 'instruction' a specific coded or emblematic meaning beyond 'God's word/teaching/discipline' would be going beyond mainstream published interpretation. The overlap of torah ('law' vs. 'instruction') also produces translation-driven variation across traditions rather than genuinely competing symbolic schools."}
